Chord Chord (by Tom's Line) browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal Chord (by Tom's Line) OD50 Overdrive/Distortion Published on November 27, 2023 Chord (by Tom's Line) distortion overdrive pedal Information Chord Description: A versatile overdrive pedal for guitar with separate Gain, Tone and Level controls. A wide range of tones are available from natural and open-sounding mild drive tones to heavier saturated distortion with all points in between to cover different music styles. Features: Gain, Tone and Level adjustment 9V battery or optional DC adaptor operation Specifications: Power supply 9V battery (PP3 included) or optional DC adaptor Construction Aluminium housing with rubber base Controls Gain, Tone and Level Dimensions 115 x 68 x 47mm Weight 275g The Chord OD50 Overdrive/Distortion, developed in collaboration with Tom's Line Engineering, is a compact analog guitar effects pedal designed to combine overdrive and distortion characteristics in a single unit. Its circuitry employs a high-gain FET transistor stage to emulate the warm, harmonically rich response of an overdriven tube amplifier. This design enables a tonal range from smooth, open-sounding overdrive to tight, saturated distortion, providing ample flexibility for rock, blues, and modern guitar tones. The pedal's response is dynamic and amp-like, with a natural compression at higher gain levels and clear note articulation across its drive spectrum. The OD50 delivers a consistent, low-noise performance through an ultra low noise operational amplifier and true bypass switching, ensuring the guitar's clean tone remains unaffected when the pedal is disengaged. Its aluminum housing with rubber base provides durability for studio and stage use, while the LED indicator shows active operation and battery status. Power options include a standard 9V battery or external 9V DC adaptor with center-negative polarity. The Chord OD50 shares its core design with the Tom's Line Engineering AOD-1, reflecting their identical analog drive architecture, control layout, and specifications.
